title: Security & viruses
blurb: Viruses, scam pop-ups, firewall, encryption, safe browsing.

remedies.title: Someone called saying they're from Microsoft, Apple or my bank
remedies.why: Real companies don't call to fix your computer or ask you to install remote-access apps.

steps.text: Hang up. Call the company back on a number from their real website or your card.
If you installed a remote app (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, etc.) for them, uninstall it and disconnect from the internet.
If you gave bank details or passwords, call your bank and change passwords from another device.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT if this happened on a work computer.

remedies.title: I found a USB stick: should I plug it in?
remedies.why: Unknown USB devices can carry malware or pretend to be a keyboard.

steps.text: Don't plug it in. Hand it to IT or lost property.

remedies.title: Is it safe to use public Wi-Fi?
remedies.why: Most sites are encrypted now, but fake hotspots and file sharing are risks.

steps.text: Mark it as a Public network so file sharing stays off.
Use the work VPN for work; check site addresses carefully.
Use your phone's hotspot for anything sensitive.

remedies.title: My email was in a data breach
remedies.why: A site you used leaked passwords; attackers try them on other sites.

steps.text: Change the password on that site and anywhere you used the same one.
Turn on two-step sign-in for email, bank and work accounts.
Use a password manager so every site has its own password.

remedies.title: A website says my browser or Flash needs updating
symptoms: your browser is out of date site
remedies.why: Websites that push "updates" are a common way to install malware. Real updates come from the browser or system itself.

steps.text: Close the page; don't download anything from it.
Update only through the browser's own menu (Help › About) or system updates.
If you ran the download, run a full scan and tell IT.

remedies.title: Lock my computer when I step away
remedies.why: An unlocked computer lets anyone nearby read your mail or act as you.

steps.text: Windows+L locks instantly. Dynamic lock locks when your paired phone walks away.
Ctrl+⌘+Q locks; set "Require password after screen saver" to immediately.
